applicable_conditions: When the enemy has air superiority fighters or long-range SAMs that can engage before weapon release.
When the mission requires J-15s to deliver weapons on target, and they are launched late relative to surface attacks.
When J-15 flight time is short (~45s) giving minimal exposure but also minimal time to reach launch distance.
counter_conditions: If the J-15s are escorted by fighters or fly a terrain-masking route that avoids detection until terminal.
If the enemy air defenses are degraded by preceding missile strikes.
If the J-15s are armed with standoff weapons that can be launched outside the interception range.
hypothesis: J-15 aircraft are highly vulnerable to interception before they can launch weapons, especially when launched with short delay and low-altitude ingress, leading to zero weapon effectiveness; thus, relying on J-15s for any critical damage is risky unless their survival is improved.

details: Step 1: Launch surface missile strikes first to degrade enemy SAM and fighter patrols.
Step 2: Launch J-15s after a 1-2 minute delay when defenses are focused on inbound missiles.
Step 3: Use high-altitude flight (e.g., 15,000 ft) and launch anti-ship missiles at max range to reduce time in lethal envelope.
recommended_pattern.summary: Delay J-15 launch until surface missiles have suppressed air defenses, and consider higher-altitude ingress with standoff launches to reduce interception likelihood.
